messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Sev2 - Increased 429s observed for /v1/generate across multiple regions. Affected org: AcmeCorp (org_id: org_0a1b2c). Start time ~ 2026-02-24T15:20:00Z. Incident page: https://redwood/incident/INC-20260224-ACME-429

alex kim: saw the first spike at 15:18 UTC, rate of 429s jumped from <0.1% to ~8% in eu-west1. CPU on shared pool nodes also spiked. Sample errors: 
```
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","detail":"org org_0a1b2c exceeded application rate quota"}
```

michael chen: tagging in. Metrics: requests/s for org_0a1b2c went from 200 -> 2k in ~2m. KV cache hit unchanged. Looks like a traffic surge from a bot loop.

alex kim: quick ask: should we apply org-level emergency throttle (limit) or temporarily bump Acme's quota on Dedicated? Both have tradeoffs. If we bump quota they won't see errors but we risk overspending / collateral impact.

julia (cs): Acme is a paying customer on Growth plan, very sensitive. CS is getting complaints from their SREs already. They asked for a temporary lift if it prevents errors.

michael chen: propose two-step hotfix: 1) immediate per-org burst cap to reduce tail 429s for other tenants, 2) create a temporary ephemeral override for Acme to keep their sessions alive while we throttle noisy tokens.

sara patel: I can run the per-org change. Suggest command via Admin API to set a short windowed override: 
```
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood/api/orgs/org_0a1b2c/rate_limits" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"window_seconds":60,"burst":500,"sustained":150,"reason":"emergency spike 2026-02-24"}'
```

alex kim: note: burst 500 sustained 150 for 60s window is higher than normal (normal sustained=50). That should reduce user-facing 429s while keeping upper bound. Monitor cost.

ops-oncall: adding ops-oncall to monitor infra cost and GPU usage. I'll toggle autoscale policies to avoid accidental overprovision.

michael chen: I'll also add a temporary routing rule to move Acme traffic to the dedicated pool for the next 15m: 
```
POST /routing/overrides {"org_id":"org_0a1b2c","target_pool":"dedicated-acme-temp","ttl":900}
```

julia (cs): Please send a short note to Acme SRE about mitigation and ETA. I'll take customer comms once it's stable. Message: "Temporary quota adjustment + routing applied; monitoring closely; we'll follow up with post-incident summary."

sara patel: applying org-level override now.

sara patel: Done. Admin response: {"status":"ok","applied_to":"org_0a1b2c","burst":500,"sustained":150,"expires_at":"2026-02-24T15:35:00Z"} :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Hotfix deployed: rate-limit-override/org_0a1b2c at 1768600106 by sara.p :rocket:

michael chen: routing override applied to dedicated-acme-temp. Confirmed 200 requests/s on dedicated nodes for Acme.

alex kim: early metrics: 429s for Acme dropped from 8% -> 0.4% within 90s. Other tenants' 429s returned to baseline.

ops-oncall: cost watch — provisioning increased by ~1.8x for the dedicated pool during the first 3m; estimated incremental cost $220 for current 15m window.

julia (cs): Acme responded: "Thanks — saw immediate reduction in errors. Please keep us posted." They asked for ETA to revert.

michael chen: plan: keep override for 15m, then rollback unless we see more surge. If surge continues, we'll propose a negotiated temporary quota extension with billing.

alex kim: handoff — I'll be off for next 30m. @sara patel, please take lead on monitoring and rollback. If anything regresses, page me.

sara patel: taking over monitoring. I have dashboard links and alerts set. Will post status updates every 5min.

sara patel: 15:28 UTC — still stable, 429s ~0.3%, dedicated pool CPU 62%.

sara patel: 15:35 UTC — override expired (automatic). Admin response: {"status":"expired","org_id":"org_0a1b2c","expired_at":"2026-02-24T15:35:00Z"}

sara patel: After expiry, error rate held at 0.6% for Acme (acceptable). No further action taken.

michael chen: I'll open a post-incident task to add finer-grained per-token throttles and automated transient overrides for known customers to avoid manual hotfixes.

alex kim: actionable items: 1) postmortem + timeline (michael) 2) engineering: automated per-org emergency overrides (P0) 3) billing: reconcile temporary overage with Acme (julia) 4) product: evaluate routing policy to prefer dedicated under sudden spikes.

julia (cs): I'll coordinate billing and reply to Acme with a note and next steps.

incident-bot: Incident resolved — Sev2 lowered. Root cause suspected bot loop from Acme integrations. Postmortem created: https://redwood/incident/INC-20260224-ACME-429/postmortem :white_check_mark:

sara patel: closing thread, handing back to on-call rotation. :wave:
